paper.title: A Taxonomy-Driven Cryptographic Dependency Inventory for Post-Quantum Migration in Decentralized Systems: Triage Rules and a Worked Example
paper.abstract: Advances in quantum computing pressure widely deployed public- key primitives (e.g., RSA, ECDSA, (EC)DH), turning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migration from an algorithm swap into a system deployment and interoperability challenge. Decentralized systems—including blockchains and Layer-2 protocols—add fric- tion via governance-driven upgrades, monetized verification, and long-lived public logs. We propose a compact migration framework: (1) a component taxonomy, (2) a cryptographic dependency inventory (CDI) schema, and (3) rule-based priority assignment (P0–P3) derived directly from CDI fields. A worked example (wallet signing, node-to-node secure channels, state commitments) illustrates how a shared inventory artifact yields actionable migration priorities without new experiments. Proof-system stacks follow the same schema but are left as an optional extension beyond this extended abstract.
